original.summary: King of Babylon. Kings and Jeremiah describe his siege of Jerusalem, Jeconiah's captivity and the removal of temple vessels. His officers later burn the temple. Daniel describes his troubling dream of a statue and his promotion of Daniel over the wise men. He makes a gold image and orders three Judean men thrown into a furnace, then praises their God. Daniel also describes him living apart from people and eating grass like oxen. He later raises his eyes to heaven and praises its King. Cyrus returns the temple vessels he had taken. Daniel's father language about Belshazzar does not establish a biological link here.

draft.summary: King of Babylon. Kings and Jeremiah describe his siege of Jerusalem, Jeconiah's captivity and the removal of temple vessels. His officers later burn the temple. Daniel describes his troubling dream of a statue and his promotion of Daniel over the wise men. He makes a gold image and orders three Judean men thrown into a furnace, then praises their God. Daniel also describes him living apart from people and eating grass like oxen. He later raises his eyes to heaven and praises its King. Cyrus returns the temple vessels he had taken. Daniel calls Nebuchadnezzar Belshazzar's father. This wording does not establish a biological link here.
